output.reason: A 60-year-old with sudden slurred speech and right facial droop lasting about 10 minutes, starting roughly 45 minutes ago, describes a likely TIA or minor stroke requiring immediate emergency evaluation even though symptoms have resolved.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 now. Sudden slurred speech with facial drooping, even when it clears up in minutes, can be a warning stroke, and the next hours carry the highest risk of a full stroke. Do not drive yourself and do not wait for a message reply. If symptoms return or new weakness, numbness or vision trouble starts, tell the dispatcher immediately.
differential: Minor ischemic stroke with resolved deficit
